banner: 被指打压开源，Anthropic 正面澄清
banner_en: Accused of blocking open weights, Anthropic answers

image.caption: 本期头条配图：Anthropic 官方博客文章《Our position on open-weights models》的标题页。CEO Dario Amodei 在文中说清楚三件事：从没主张过封杀开源模型，真正想卡住的是对华芯片出口和工业化蒸馏，以及要求所有强模型不分开源闭源都过安全测试。（图：Anthropic 官方博客）
image.caption_en: This issue's lead image: the title page of Anthropic's blog post "Our position on open-weights models." CEO Dario Amodei spells out three things: he has never advocated banning open-weight models, what he actually wants restricted is chip exports to China and industrial-scale distillation, and all capable models, open or closed, should go through safety testing. (Image: Anthropic's official blog.)

actions.text: 今晚花十五分钟，测一下自己产品里那个需要模型做判断的功能（内容审核、客服话术、简历筛选、评论打标签之类），看默认立场会不会让用户意外。今天 unslop.run 那份测试显示，16 个主流大模型里 15 个都落在同一个政治象限，跟模型是开源还是闭源、产地在哪个国家几乎没关系。具体做法：挑三到五个你的产品会遇到的、有争议但能验证对错的问题，直接问一遍你在用的模型，再把同一个问题正着问反着问各来一遍（比如“A 比 B 好”和“B 比 A 好”），看回答会不会只因为措辞方向变了就跟着翻转。如果翻转了，说明模型给的不是真判断，是顺着题目说话的从众偏差，这种功能上线前最好再核实一遍。
actions.source: Hacker News · 给16个大模型做政治罗盘测试
actions.text_en: Tonight, spend fifteen minutes testing whether the AI-judgment feature in your own product (content moderation, support scripting, resume screening, comment tagging) has a default stance that would surprise your users. A test published today on unslop.run ran 16 major LLMs through the Political Compass and found 15 of them land in the same political quadrant, almost regardless of whether the model is open or closed, or where it was built. Concretely: pick three to five contested-but-checkable questions your product actually runs into, ask the model you use directly, then ask the same question in both directions ("A is better than B" and "B is better than A") and see if the answer just flips because the phrasing flipped. If it does, that's acquiescence bias talking, not a real judgment, and it's worth verifying before that feature ships.
actions.source_en: Hacker News · Political Compass test on 16 LLMs

actions.text: 今晚花十分钟，找出你自己产品或工具里调用最频繁、判断标准相对固定的那一个 LLM 环节（分类、打标签、审核之类），记录下最近 20 到 30 条真实的输入和输出。今天 Hacker News 上一篇文章（由一家做强化学习微调服务的公司发布，数字未经第三方核实）给出一个具体案例：电商平台的商品目录审核，用一个 500 美元训练出来的 90 亿参数开源模型，跑分反而超过所有测过的前沿模型，每条审核成本从 34 美元/千条降到 0.5 美元/千条。具体做法：不用现在就去微调模型，先把这 20 到 30 条真实数据存下来，这就是将来如果要做专属小模型时最需要的种子数据，现在攒比到时候补容易得多。
actions.source: Hacker News · 500美元强化学习微调跑赢前沿模型
actions.text_en: Tonight, spend ten minutes finding the single most frequent, most fixed-criteria LLM step in your own product or tools (classification, tagging, review) and log 20 to 30 real inputs and outputs from it. A Hacker News post today (published by a company that sells RL fine-tuning services, numbers not independently verified) gives a concrete case: an e-commerce catalog-review workflow where a $500 GRPO fine-tune of a 9B open model outscored every frontier model tested, cutting per-listing cost from $34 per 1,000 to $0.50 per 1,000. Concretely: you don't need to fine-tune anything tonight, just save those 20 to 30 real examples. That's the seed dataset a specialist model would eventually train on, and it's far easier to collect now than to backfill later.
actions.source_en: Hacker News · $500 RL fine-tune beats frontier models

actions.text: 今晚花十分钟，把你产品里那个“AI 真的在替用户干活、不只是辅助”的功能挑出来，算一下如果按它帮用户省下的钱或者省下的时间抽成，而不是按账号数收订阅费，价格会长什么样。今天 TechCrunch 报道的 Prentis（Reid Hoffman 和 Mark Pincus 新开的电脑操作 agent 公司，正在洽谈 1 亿美元融资）就是这么定价的：不卖订阅，从帮客户省下的钱里抽 20%。具体做法：挑一个你能大致估算“省了多少”的功能，比如替用户少做几步操作、少花多少时间，写一个“按省下来的钱抽 X%”的定价方案草稿，跟现在的订阅价格比一比，哪个对愿意用满这个功能的重度用户更划算。
actions.source: 文摘 · Prentis：卖省下的钱，不卖订阅（经 TLDR AI 精选）
actions.text_en: Tonight, spend ten minutes picking out the one feature in your product where the AI is genuinely doing the work for a user, not just assisting, and roughly price what it would look like if you charged a cut of the money or time it saves instead of a per-seat subscription. TechCrunch reported today that Prentis, a new computer-use agent startup co-founded by Reid Hoffman and Mark Pincus that's in talks to raise $100M, prices exactly this way: no subscription, a 20% cut of whatever it saves the customer. Concretely: pick a feature where you can roughly estimate the savings, sketch a "take X% of the savings" pricing draft, and compare it to your current subscription price to see which one makes more sense for a heavy user who actually uses the feature to the fullest.
actions.source_en: Digest · Prentis: selling savings, not subscriptions (curated via TLDR AI)

hands_on.title: 今晚 10 分钟：把手机 ChatGPT 切到 Work 模式，试一次联网版代码解释器
hands_on.why: Simon Willison 今天点评 Ethan Mollick 的 AI 工具指南时提了一个很少人知道的细节：手机上的 ChatGPT，默认的 Chat 模式和切换过去的 Work 模式，背后的代码解释器权限不一样，切到 Work 模式之后，代码解释器就能访问互联网，桌面版反而没有这个差异。这是一个不用装任何东西、现在手机上就能试的小改动，正好用来感受一下“给 AI 多开一点权限”到底会带来什么实际差别。
steps: 打开手机上的 ChatGPT App，确认自己在用的账号有 Work 模式（目前部分订阅层级才有）
把对话模式从默认的 Chat 切换到 Work
让它跑一个需要联网查资料再处理的小任务，比如“查一下今天旧金山的天气，再帮我把这个温度换算成华氏度”
回到 Chat 模式再问一遍同样的问题，对比两次它有没有主动联网、结果是不是不一样
留意这中间有没有哪一步让你意外，这就是“模式命名混乱”背后真正该在意的地方
hands_on.source: 文摘 · Simon Willison 点评 Ethan Mollick 的AI工具指南
hands_on.title_en: Tonight, 10 minutes: flip ChatGPT mobile to Work mode and try its internet-connected Code Interpreter
hands_on.why_en: Commenting today on Ethan Mollick's AI tool guide, Simon Willison flagged a detail few people know: on mobile ChatGPT, the default Chat mode and the Work mode you can switch to carry different Code Interpreter permissions, and flipping to Work mode gives the Code Interpreter internet access that the desktop app doesn't have this way. It's a small change you can test on your phone right now with nothing to install, and a good way to actually feel what "giving the AI a bit more access" changes in practice.
steps_en: Open the ChatGPT app on your phone and confirm your account has Work mode (currently limited to some subscription tiers)
Switch the conversation mode from the default Chat to Work
Give it a small task that needs to look something up online and then process it, like "check today's weather in San Francisco and convert that temperature to Fahrenheit"
Switch back to Chat mode and ask the same question, comparing whether it goes online on its own and whether the answer differs
Notice whether any step surprises you. That's the part of the confusing mode names actually worth paying attention to
hands_on.source_en: Digest · Simon Willison on Ethan Mollick's AI tool guide

meta_read: 今天声音最大的新闻是一场关于谁有资格决定 AI 该不该开放的政治仗：英伟达牵头的联署信一天内翻倍到 50 家，逼得被点名的 Anthropic 亲自下场澄清自己从没主张过封杀开源模型。这场仗吵得响，但把今天另外几条放在一起看，会发现真正决定 AI 怎么被用起来的，可能根本不是开源还是闭源这个轴。第一，经济账已经有人算完了：一家做微调服务的公司晒出案例，500 美元训练出来的 90 亿参数开源模型，在电商目录审核这个具体任务上跑赢了所有前沿模型，成本只要几十分之一，说明企业不用等政策吵出结果，早就在用自己的数据把这道题的答案做出来了。第二，开源本身也不保证价值观更中立：一份测了 16 个模型的研究显示，不管模型来自美国、欧洲还是中国，不管开源闭源，15 个都落在同一个政治象限，模型的立场看起来更像是训练数据和对齐方式决定的，跟权重公不公开关系不大。第三，就算是目前公认最强的闭源模型，可靠性这道题也还没过关：Opus 5 在一个模拟真实项目需求边写边加的编程基准上，通过率也只有 24%，说明限制企业真正把 AI 用起来的，往往不是能不能拿到模型权重，而是模型到底靠不靠谱。这三条放在一起说明，开源联署信吵得越凶，越衬出这场仗本身可能押错了轴：真正决定谁能把 AI 用出效益的，是谁先把自己的任务数据和评测跑出来，谁先想清楚该收订阅费还是该按省下来的钱抽成，而不是谁先在联署信上签了名。
meta_read_en: Today's loudest story is a political fight over who gets to decide whether AI should stay open: Nvidia's coalition letter doubled to 50 signatories in a day, forcing Anthropic, which got named as the villain, to step in and clarify it never called for banning open-weight models. That fight is loud, but line up today's other items and the real lever deciding how AI gets used may not be the open-versus-closed axis at all. First, someone has already run the economics: a fine-tuning vendor's case study shows a $500 training run on a 9B open model beating every frontier model tested on e-commerce catalog review, at a fraction of the cost, meaning companies aren't waiting for the policy fight to resolve, they're already answering the question with their own data. Second, openness itself doesn't guarantee neutral values: a study testing 16 models found 15 of them land in the same political quadrant regardless of whether they're open or closed or built in the US, Europe, or China, suggesting a model's stance comes from its training data and alignment process, not from whether its weights are public. Third, even the strongest closed frontier model hasn't solved reliability: Opus 5 only clears 24% of a coding benchmark that simulates a real project's requirements changing as work proceeds, meaning what actually limits a company's real AI deployment is often not access to weights but whether the model can be trusted. Put together, the louder the open-weights letter gets, the more it looks like the fight is being fought on the wrong axis. What actually decides who gets value out of AI is who gets their own task data and evaluation running first, and who figures out whether to charge a subscription or a cut of the savings, not who signs the letter first.

learned: 读台账确认，过去十一条主线基本都在“怎么运行、怎么写好一个多 agent 循环”这条轴上打转（评测分级、效果分层、供应商容错、证据分级、harness 可移植性审计、技能瘦身）。今天 unslop.run 那份政治罗盘测试提供了一个具体的方法论缺口：测 16 个模型时，除了正着问一遍，还专门设计了“把题目正反颠倒问一遍”和“把题目顺序打乱重排”两组对照，用来把模型真实的判断和顺着题目措辞从众这两件事分开。这跟 07-19 晚间那条“裁决给不出可核查理由就当 unsure”的门槛是同一个方向，但补的是一个更具体的检测手段：不是靠模型自己说我确定，而是靠反着问一遍，看答案会不会只因为措辞方向变了就跟着翻。

回头看我自己现在写的评测/裁判类 prompt（不管是这份 daily-digest 里给发现或结论打通过/不通过，还是任何用模型当 judge 的场景），基本没有做这种镜像反问的对照，只是单次问一遍就采信。这个具体缺口值得补进 07-19 晚间那条 abstention-aware eval gates 里，作为一种新增的检测手段：给出裁决的模型，除了要给可核查理由，还应该被反着问一遍同一件事，如果答案只因为措辞方向变了就翻转、理由却站不住，这条裁决就该按 unsure 处理，而不是采信。
new_capabilities: “镜像反问：给每个当裁判用的 judge prompt 加一次极性反转的对照” 云端提议，待笔记本采纳。具体做法：任何时候需要一个模型对某件事下判断（这份工作里最常见的是给一个发现或结论打通过/不通过），除了正着问一遍，再把陈述的极性反过来问一遍（比如把“X 是对的”换成“X 是错的”），如果两次回答只因为极性反转就跟着完全翻转、并且给不出新的、独立于措辞本身的理由，就把这次裁决标记为 unsure，交给下一级处理，不要采信。这不是重复 07-19 晚间那条“裁决要给可核查理由”的门槛，而是给它补一个具体、可执行的检测方法，灵感来自今天 unslop.run 政治罗盘测试里“正反颠倒问一遍、排除从众偏差”的实验设计。调用意图：“给任何当裁判用的 judge 加一次镜像反问，如果结论只因为措辞方向变了就翻转，标记为 unsure，别采信。”
learned_en: Reading the ledger, the last eleven lines all sit on one axis: how to run and write a good multi-agent loop (binary evals, effort tiering, provider fail-over, evidence grading, harness-portability audits, skill diet). Today's Political Compass test on 16 LLMs from unslop.run surfaces a concrete methodological gap: alongside the straight run, the author specifically added a reversed-statement pass and a reordered pass to separate a model's genuine judgment from acquiescence bias, agreeing with whatever direction a statement is phrased in. That's the same direction as 07-19 evening's line (a verdict with no checkable reason gets treated as unsure), but it adds a concrete detection method: instead of trusting a model's own claimed confidence, ask the mirrored version of the same question and see if the answer just flips.

Looking back at the eval/judge prompts I actually write, whether it's grading a finding or conclusion as pass/fail in this very daily-digest workflow or any other scenario using a model as judge, none of them currently run this mirrored-question check, they just ask once and take the answer. This specific gap is worth folding into 07-19 evening's abstention-aware eval gates line as a new detection method: a model issuing a verdict should also be asked the mirrored version of the same question, and if the answer flips just because the phrasing's polarity flipped with no independent reason, that verdict should be treated as unsure, not trusted.
new_capabilities_en: 🎯 (cloud-proposed, pending laptop adoption) "Mirror-question check: add a polarity-reversed pass to every judge prompt": concretely, whenever a model is asked to render a verdict on something (most commonly in this work, passing or failing a finding or conclusion), ask it once straight and once with the statement's polarity reversed (e.g., swap "X is correct" for "X is incorrect"), and if the two answers simply flip along with the polarity with no new reason independent of the phrasing, mark that verdict as unsure and hand it to the next escalation level rather than trusting it. This doesn't repeat 07-19 evening's line that a verdict needs a checkable reason; it adds a concrete, runnable detection method for one specific way that requirement gets gamed, inspired by today's Political Compass test's reversed-and-reordered experimental design for ruling out acquiescence bias. Invoke intent: "add a mirror-question pass to any judge call; if the verdict flips only because the phrasing's polarity flipped, mark it unsure and don't trust it."

items.title: 遭指控主张封杀开源模型，Anthropic CEO正面回应
items.title_en: Accused of wanting to ban open-weight models, Anthropic's CEO responds
items.author: Dario Amodei · Anthropic官方博客 · Hacker News
items.author_en: Dario Amodei · Anthropic official blog · Hacker News
items.flag: ⚠️ HN 评论区不少人认为这篇声明本身也是利益相关方的表态：Anthropic 是全球估值最高的闭源模型公司之一，反对“禁令”的同时又主张对所有强模型做强制安全测试，客观上同样会抬高开源模型的合规门槛。声明里的论点是 Dario 一方之词，不是中立结论。
items.flag_en: ⚠️ Many HN commenters point out that this statement itself comes from an interested party: Anthropic is one of the most valuable closed-model companies in the world, and while it opposes a ban, its push for mandatory safety testing on all sufficiently capable models would also raise the compliance bar facing open models. Read Dario's arguments as one side's case, not a neutral verdict.
items.summary: 过去几天，该不该限制开源模型这个话题突然吵起来了，导火索是华盛顿有官员在考虑禁止美国公司使用中国的开源模型。英伟达牵头，联合微软、Meta、IBM、Palantir、a16z、Hugging Face 等发了一封联署信反对这类限制，7 月 24 日发布时只有 25 家签署，第二天就翻倍到 50 家，OpenAI 和谷歌后来也加入了，黄仁勋自己在 X 上发的帖子几小时内看了 1100 万次。但联署名单里始终没有 Anthropic 和亚马逊，两家都没公开解释原因。Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei 就在这个背景下写了这篇声明，说有人借这次讨论指责 Anthropic 想封杀开源模型，他要把话说清楚：Anthropic 从来没有主张过禁止开源模型，没有危险能力的开源模型是公共品，只需要付得起算力就能用，对企业、开发者、研究者都有价值。他说自己真正担心的是两件事：一是集权国家（不只是中国，但中国是目前能力最强的那个）造出比美国更强的模型，用来谋求军事优势或者镇压本国人民，这件事跟模型是不是开源、是不是被美国公司使用完全无关，最危险的模型甚至可能是被秘密训练、只交给军队和情报部门用的那种；二是模型被用来搞网络攻击或者生物武器，或者模型本身有对齐问题。针对这两个担忧，他提出三项具体措施：卡住高端芯片和芯片制造设备卖给中国，同时打击绕开管制的走私行为；打击工业化规模的蒸馏行为（蒸馏能让中国用比自己芯片数量该有的能力更强的模型，但蒸馏本身跟开源与否无关，问题是背后有没有国家力量在推）；要求所有足够强的模型，不管开源闭源，发布前都过网络安全、生物安全和对齐风险的强制测试。对英伟达那封联署信，他说自己同意大部分内容，开源模型确实能扩大准入、增强竞争、给客户更多控制权，但不同意信里说的开源必然更容易做安全防护、或者能力扩散对防守方比进攻方更有利，他举例说生物武器领域很可能恰恰相反，模型足够强的话，武器化一个大流行级别病毒可能只需要很短时间，而防御这类武器往往是跨年度的系统工程。
items.summary_en: Over the past few days the question of whether open-weight models should be restricted suddenly caught fire, sparked by reports that Washington officials were considering banning US companies from using Chinese open-weight models. Nvidia led a coalition with Microsoft, Meta, IBM, Palantir, a16z, and Hugging Face, among others, in a letter opposing such restrictions, published July 24 with 25 signatories that doubled to 50 the next day, with OpenAI and Google joining later, and Jensen Huang's own post on X racking up 11 million views within hours. But Anthropic and Amazon never appeared on the list, and neither has publicly explained why. It's against that backdrop that Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei wrote this statement, saying some people have used the moment to accuse Anthropic of wanting to ban open-weight models, and he wants to set the record straight: Anthropic has never advocated banning open-weight models, since models without dangerous capabilities are a public good that costs nothing beyond compute and provides value to businesses, developers, and researchers. He says his real concerns are two nightmare scenarios: authoritarian governments (not only China, though China is the most capable) building models more powerful than the US's and using them for military superiority or domestic repression, something that has nothing to do with whether a model is open or used by US businesses, since the most dangerous model might be one trained in secret and handed only to the military and intelligence services; and powerful models being misused for cyberattacks or bioweapons, or having serious alignment problems. To address these, he proposes three concrete measures: block the sale of advanced chips and chipmaking equipment to China while cracking down on smuggling that evades the controls; crack down on industrial-scale distillation operations (distillation lets China build far more capable models than its chip count would otherwise allow, though distillation itself has nothing to do with openness, the real issue is state power behind the operation); and require all sufficiently capable models, open or closed, to pass mandatory cyber, biological, and alignment safety testing before release. On Nvidia's letter, he says he agrees with most of it, since open-weight models do expand access, strengthen competition, and give customers more control, but he disagrees with the letter's claims that openness necessarily makes safeguards easier to build or that broader access helps defenders more than attackers, arguing biology may well run the opposite way, since a sufficiently capable model could weaponize a pandemic-level virus quickly while defending against one is typically a multi-year undertaking.
items.why: 本期头条，也是这几天谁能决定 AI 该不该开放这场争论里最直接的一次正面交锋：一边是英伟达牵头、一天内翻倍到 50 家公司的联署信，一边是被点名涉嫌想禁开源的 Anthropic 亲自下场澄清立场。可迁移的判断：读这类声明时，别只看结论，去看它同意联署信哪几条、反对哪几条，反对的那部分往往才是真正的利益交锋点。今晚能做的事，去看看联署信本身翻倍的速度和缺席名单能读出什么（详见文摘版）。
items.why_en: The issue's lead, and the most direct head-on clash in the past few days' fight over who gets to decide whether AI should stay open: on one side a Nvidia-led letter that doubled to 50 companies in a day, on the other Anthropic, accused of wanting to ban open weights, stepping in to clarify its own position. The transferable judgment: when reading a statement like this, don't just look at the conclusion, look at which parts of the opposing letter it agrees with and which it rejects. The rejected parts are usually where the real interests collide. Tonight's move: see what the letter's own doubling speed and absentee list reveal (see the Digest section).

items.title: SlopCodeBench 实测：Opus 5 写的代码量翻三倍，但过关率仍只有24%
items.title_en: SlopCodeBench results: Opus 5 writes 3x more code but still only clears 24% of checkpoints
items.author: HumanLayer 团队 · Hacker News
items.flag: ⚠️ 作者只测了 17 个检查点、3 道题目的子集，不是完整跑一遍原论文的全部题库，样本量偏小；代码质量差 11.6 倍这类具体倍数，是作者自己拿 slop 检测规则去套 TypeScript 代码算出来的，不是第三方复现的结果。
items.flag_en: ⚠️ The author only tested a 17-checkpoint, 3-problem subset, not a full re-run of the original paper's whole problem set, so the sample is small. Specific multiples like 11.6x more quality warnings come from the author's own adaptation of slop-detection rules to TypeScript, not an independently replicated result.
items.summary: SlopCodeBench 是威斯康星大学麦迪逊分校提出的一个长周期编程基准。与常见的一次性给出全部需求的跑分不同，它把软件项目的需求拆成多个检查点，边推进边追加新需求，模拟真实项目中需求不断变化的情形。原论文中，GPT-5.4 和 Opus 4.6 在这个基准上的严格通过率分别只有 11% 和 17%，远未被刷满。本文作者用 Opus 5、Opus 4.8、Sonnet 5 三个模型，在 3 道题目、17 个检查点的子集上重新测试：Opus 5 通过 4 个，通过率 24%，仅比论文中 Opus 4.6 的 17% 略高；Opus 4.8 和 Sonnet 5 各只通过 1 个，通过率 6%。代码量方面，Opus 5 写了 29065 行源代码，是其他模型（约 9000 行）的三倍多，但其中 51% 是测试代码（Opus 4.8 仅 11%）。作者称之为“昂贵的啰嗦”——代码量大增，正确率却没跟上。复杂度方面，Opus 4.8 随检查点推进复杂度上升 70%，Opus 5 基本持平，但 Opus 5 写的函数数量是其他模型的 5 倍，其中 14.9% 仅被调用一次（Sonnet 5 为 71.5%），说明几个模型拆分代码的风格截然不同。作者还将代码质量检测规则套用到 TypeScript 上，发现 Opus 5 生成的代码每千行触发 178.88 条质量警告，是作者维护的生产代码库（15.06 条/千行）的 11.6 倍。作者结论：这个基准首次把原来只能凭感觉的判断量化出来。对于真实的软件工程——逐个处理具体问题而非一次性给全需求——今天的模型还不能信任“关灯自动跑”，需要人工监督。
items.summary_en: SlopCodeBench is a long-horizon coding benchmark from UW Madison that, unlike a typical one-shot benchmark handing over all requirements upfront, splits a software project's requirements into multiple checkpoints and adds new ones as work proceeds, simulating how requirements keep shifting on a real project. The original paper found GPT-5.4 and Opus 4.6 clearing only 11% and 17% strict pass rates respectively, making it a far-from-saturated benchmark. This post's author re-ran Opus 5, Opus 4.8, and Sonnet 5 on a subset of 3 problems and 17 checkpoints: Opus 5 passed 4 of 17, a 24% pass rate only marginally above the paper's Opus 4.6 baseline of 17%, while Opus 4.8 and Sonnet 5 each passed just 1, a 6% rate. On code volume, Opus 5 wrote 29,065 lines of source code, more than three times the roughly 9,000 lines from the other models, but 51% of it was test code (versus 11% for Opus 4.8), which the author calls expensive verbosity, more code without proportionally more correctness. On complexity, Opus 4.8's cyclomatic complexity grew 70% across checkpoints while Opus 5's stayed roughly flat, though Opus 5 wrote five times as many functions as the others, with 14.9% of them single-use (versus 71.5% for Sonnet 5), suggesting very different decomposition styles. Adapting slop-detection rules to TypeScript, the author found Opus 5's code triggered 178.88 quality warnings per thousand lines, 11.6 times the 15.06 per thousand in the author's own carefully maintained production codebase. The author's conclusion: this benchmark finally quantifies something that used to be anecdotal, that for real-shaped software engineering work done one issue at a time rather than handed over all at once, today's models still can't be trusted to run lights-off without a human watching.
items.why: 与头条形成互补：头条讨论谁有资格决定 AI 该不该开放，本条则指出，无论开源闭源，模型本身的可靠性问题尚未解决。Opus 5 作为当前最强闭源模型之一，在该基准上也仅通过 24%。可迁移的判断：评估编程 agent 时，不要只看官方跑分或代码量，而应观察它在需求逐步追加这类更真实场景下的表现。测试代码占比、函数复用率等细节往往比通过率本身更能说明问题。
items.why_en: This complements the lead: the lead is about who gets to decide whether AI stays open, while this is a reminder that regardless of open or closed, model reliability itself isn't solved, and Opus 5, one of today's strongest closed models, still only clears 24% of this benchmark. The transferable judgment: when judging whether a coding agent is actually good, don't just look at official benchmarks or lines of code, look at whether it holds up as requirements get added mid-project, where details like test-code ratio and function reuse rate often say more than the raw pass rate.

items.title: 电商巨头悄悄在做的事：500美元的强化学习微调，跑赢所有前沿模型
items.title_en: What e-commerce giants are quietly doing: a $500 RL fine-tune beats every frontier model
items.author: Fermisense（AI 微调服务商）· Hacker News
items.author_en: Fermisense (an AI fine-tuning vendor) · Hacker News
items.flag: ⚠️ 本文由一家专门做强化学习微调服务的公司撰写并发布。Bridgewater、Harvey、Intercom 的具体数据均引用自这些公司自己的公开表态，未经第三方复核。HN 评论区有人指出，文章给自己的评测集打分所用的评分函数，与训练模型时所用的评分函数相同——自己出题自己判的设计削弱了比较结果的说服力。也有人质疑 Ramp 那组“AI 投入越多、营收涨得越多”的数据可能因果倒置：原本营收增长快的公司，才更有预算投入 AI。
items.flag_en: ⚠️ This piece is written and published by a company that sells RL fine-tuning services, and the specific numbers cited from Bridgewater, Harvey, and Intercom come from those companies' own public statements with no independent verification. HN commenters note the scoring function used to grade the benchmark is the same one used to train the model, undercutting the comparison, and question whether the correlation in Ramp's AI-adopters-grow-faster data actually runs the other way: companies already growing faster simply have more budget to spend on AI.
items.summary: 一家做强化学习微调服务的公司发布长文，核心案例是电商平台的商品目录审核：每条商品需归类目、提取图片和文字描述中的属性，出错会导致商品搜不到、推荐变差，甚至假货蒙混过关。文章称，一个中等规模平台每天审核 1000 万条商品，若全部调用前沿模型，一年成本约 5 亿美元；改用他们用强化学习微调的一个 90 亿参数开源模型自行处理，一年约 1000 万美元，成本降幅达 98%。具体评测：他们训练的模型在目录审核任务上获得满分 87.3%，超越他们测试过的最强前沿模型配置（76.9%），比微调前的基础模型（64.2%）高 36%。五个前沿模型无论如何优化提示词，分数均卡在 76% 出头，微调后的小模型直接跳出这个天花板。每条商品的审核成本，从最贵前沿方案的 34 美元/千条，降至自己模型的 0.5 美元/千条，便宜 68 倍；即便与最便宜的前沿方案相比，也便宜 40 倍。文章还列举了另外三个类似案例：Bridgewater 用自家分析师标注的数据训练模型判断哪些文件与投资相关，错误率比最好前沿模型低 30%；法律 AI 公司 Harvey 用强化学习在开源模型上训练出的法务 agent，在其评分标准上跑赢 GPT-5.5 和 Claude Opus 4.8；Intercom 对其客服 agent Fin Apex 进行同样训练后，问题解决比例超过最好前沿模型，且成本更低。文章总结的路径是：先用前沿模型自动化跑流程，积累真实输入输出数据；待流程稳定进入量产阶段，再用这些数据配合强化学习微调一个更小的开源模型，将判断逻辑沉淀进模型权重，同时把易变的事实（价格、库存、政策文本）继续放在外部工具中查询。
items.summary_en: A company that sells RL fine-tuning services published a long piece centered on an e-commerce catalog-review case: every listing needs to land in the right taxonomy category, with attributes accurately extracted from its images and text, since getting it wrong ranges from listings becoming hard to find to counterfeit products slipping through. The piece estimates that a mid-size marketplace reviewing 10 million listings a day would spend roughly $500M a year routing everything through frontier models, versus about $10M a year running their own RL fine-tune of a 9B open model, a 98% cost reduction. On the specific scoring: their fine-tuned model reached 87.3% of the maximum score on catalog review, beating the best frontier configuration they tested (76.9%) and improving 36% over its own untrained base (64.2%); five frontier models, however optimized their prompts, all plateaued just above 76%, a ceiling the fine-tuned specialist broke through outright. Per-listing review cost dropped from $34 per 1,000 with the priciest frontier setup to $0.50 per 1,000 with their own model, 68 times cheaper, and still 40 times cheaper than the least expensive frontier option. The piece cites three similar cases: Bridgewater trained a model on its own analysts' labels to judge which documents are relevant to its investment thesis, cutting error rate 30% versus the best frontier model; legal AI company Harvey ran reinforcement learning on an open-weight model and got a legal agent that beats GPT-5.5 and Claude Opus 4.8 on its own rubrics; and Intercom trained its support agent Fin Apex the same way, resolving more issues than the best frontier models at lower cost. The playbook the piece lands on: get automation running with frontier models first to accumulate real input-output data, then once the workflow reaches production scale, use that data with reinforcement learning to fine-tune a smaller open model, baking the judgment itself into the weights while keeping facts that change (prices, inventory, policy text) in external tools.
items.why: 与头条关于谁有资格开放模型的政策争论形成鲜明对比：无论上层争议如何，企业已在悄悄用开源模型加自有数据交出自己的答案。这个 48 到 68 倍的降本案例说明，对已在实际生产环境中跑量的公司而言，“是否支持开源”早已不是需要等待政策定论的问题。可迁移的判断：如果你的产品中有某个 LLM 调用属于高频、重复、判断标准相对固定的场景（如分类、审核、打标签），这类任务正是用开源模型微调最容易见效的领域；通用型开放式任务则不适合。今晚可做的事：找出你自己产品中调用最频繁的那个 LLM 判断点（详见一版行动二）。
items.why_en: This makes a sharp contrast with the lead's policy fight over who gets to decide whether models stay open: whatever's happening up top, companies are quietly using open models plus their own data to answer the question themselves, with a concrete case showing 40 to 68x cost reduction. Whether to support open weights, for a company already running production volume, stopped being a question that waits on policy a while ago. The transferable judgment: if your product has an LLM call that's high-frequency, repetitive, and judged against relatively fixed criteria (classification, review, tagging), that's exactly where fine-tuning an open model pays off fastest, unlike open-ended general tasks. Tonight's move: find the most frequently called LLM judgment point in your own product (see Action 2).

items.title: 给16个大模型做政治罗盘测试：15个都落在“左翼自由派”象限
items.title_en: Political Compass test on 16 LLMs: 15 land in the same libertarian-left quadrant
items.author: unslop.run 独立研究者 · Hacker News
items.flag: ⚠️ 测试只用英文，强制选择，不设中立选项，题目源自 2001 年版政治罗盘测试；Claude 系列通过 Claude Code 包装调用，与直接调 API 可能有差异；不同模型采样参数未完全统一，结果仅供方向性参考。
items.flag_en: ⚠️ The test ran English-only with forced-choice questions and no neutral option, using the original 2001 Political Compass questionnaire; Claude models were queried through a Claude Code wrapper rather than directly via API, and sampling settings weren't fully standardized across providers, so treat the results as directional, not precise.
items.summary: 一位独立研究者对 16 个主流大模型进行了政治罗盘测试，覆盖美国的 ChatGPT 系列、Claude 系列、Grok 4.5，欧洲的 Mistral Large/Small，以及中国的 Kimi K2、Qwen3、GLM 4.5 等。每个模型执行 30 次完整测试、30 次题目正反颠倒（以排除从众偏差）、10 次题目顺序打乱（排除顺序效应），总计约 7 万次问答。研究者还逆向解析了 politicalcompass.org 的打分算法以核验结果。结果：16 个模型中有 15 个落在经济左翼、社会自由派象限，经济轴分数在-4.8 至-8.6 之间，社会轴在-5.0 至-7.6 之间；同一模型多次测试结果高度稳定，最大波动约 1.2 分。模型原产地影响甚微：同一国家内不同模型间的差异，反而大于国家间的差异。唯一的例外是 Grok，它会在两种人格间大致对半切换：一半概率给出经济左翼约-5.9 分的回答，另一半概率给出经济右翼约+3.3 分的回答。研究者猜测，这是训练数据与系统提示词方向相反导致的双峰分布。研究者还选取了 12 道与美国真实民调数据对应的题目进行比较，发现模型在其中 10 道题上，将美国人本已占多数的立场进一步推向几乎全体一致，仅在死刑和体罚两道题上，模型的立场与多数民意相反。此外，直接询问模型“你觉得自己政治立场偏左还是偏右”时，模型会系统性低估自身的左倾程度，平均低估 4.64 分。62 道题中，有 42 道题 16 个模型给出了完全一致的答案。
items.summary_en: An independent researcher ran the Political Compass test on 16 major LLMs, spanning the US's ChatGPT and Claude families and Grok 4.5, Europe's Mistral Large and Small, and China's Kimi K2, Qwen3, and GLM 4.5, among others. Each model ran 30 straight passes, 30 passes with statements reversed (to rule out acquiescence bias where the model just agrees with whatever way a question is phrased), and 10 passes with questions reordered (to rule out order effects), about 70,000 responses total, and the author reverse-engineered politicalcompass.org's own scoring algorithm to check accuracy. Results: 15 of 16 models landed in the economically-left, socially-liberal quadrant, with economic scores between -4.8 and -8.6 and social scores between -5.0 and -7.6, and each model was highly consistent across runs, with a maximum variance of about 1.2 points. A model's country of origin barely mattered, with variation between models from the same country exceeding variation between countries. The one exception was Grok, which split roughly 50/50 between two personas, giving an economically-left response around -5.9 about half the time and an economically-right response around +3.3 the other half, which the author suspects comes from conflicting training data and system-prompt direction producing a bimodal distribution. Comparing 12 questions against real US polling data, the author found models pushed the already-majority American position toward near-unanimous agreement on 10 of them, breaking against majority opinion only on the death penalty and corporal punishment. Asked directly whether they lean left or right, models systematically underestimated their own leftward lean by an average of 4.64 points. Of 62 propositions, 42 got identical answers across all 16 models.
items.why: 本期唯一一条提醒你开放不等于中立的条目，与前面几条关于模型是否该开放的争论形成对照：无论模型开源还是闭源、产地是美国、欧洲还是中国，训练出的政治立场竟高度趋同。这说明公众争论的“开放程度”这个轴，可能并非决定模型价值观和风险画像的关键。可迁移的判断：如果你的产品中包含模型，需要就有争议的问题进行判断或打标签，不要假设换一个更开放或更本土的模型就能拿到更中立的结果。模型的默认立场需自行测试方可得知。今晚可做的事：测试自家产品的默认立场是否会令用户意外（详见一版行动一）。
items.why_en: The issue's one item reminding you that open doesn't mean neutral, contrasting with the earlier debate over whether models should stay open: regardless of whether a model is open or closed, or built in the US, Europe, or China, its trained political stance converges to a striking degree, suggesting the openness axis everyone's fighting over may not be the axis that actually determines a model's values and risk profile. The transferable judgment: if your product has a model judging or tagging contested questions, don't assume swapping in a more open or more local model gets you a more neutral result. A model's default stance needs to be tested on its own. Tonight's move: test whether your own product's default stance would surprise users (see Action 1).

items.title: 一封联署信一天翻倍到50家，OpenAI和谷歌也签了，Anthropic和亚马逊没签
items.title_en: A coalition letter doubles to 50 signatories in a day; OpenAI and Google sign, Anthropic and Amazon don't
items.author: 英伟达 Jensen Huang 牵头（经 TLDR AI 精选）
items.author_en: Led by Nvidia's Jensen Huang (curated via TLDR AI)
items.flag: ⚠️ Anthropic 和亚马逊为何未签署，两家均未公开解释。外部报道的猜测（如保护自家闭源生意，或对开放权重的不可控性有安全顾虑）仅为猜测，非官方说法。
items.flag_en: ⚠️ Neither Anthropic nor Amazon has publicly explained why it didn't sign; outside coverage's guesses (protecting a closed-model business, or a genuine safety concern about weights you can't recall) are speculation, not an official statement.
items.summary: 7 月 24 日，英伟达牵头联合微软、Meta、IBM、Palantir、a16z、Hugging Face、Mozilla、Linux 基金会等 25 家公司，发布联署信《开放权重与美国 AI 领导力》，反对华盛顿拟议的“禁止美国公司使用（尤其是中国的）开源模型”等限制措施。核心论点是：美国要保持 AI 领先地位，应依靠开放的模型生态，而非死守某一最强模型。英伟达 CEO 黄仁勋在 X 平台发布其首条帖子推广此信，数小时内浏览量达 1100 万次。次日，签署方翻倍至 50 家，新加入者包括 OpenAI、谷歌、AMD、思科、Cloudflare、GitHub、Ollama 等。其中 OpenAI 和谷歌主营闭源模型，亦选择签署。名单中始终未出现 Anthropic 和亚马逊（亚马逊是 Anthropic 最大投资方），这两家均依赖前沿模型能力，但未公开说明未签原因。
items.summary_en: On July 24, Nvidia led Microsoft, Meta, IBM, Palantir, a16z, Hugging Face, Mozilla, and the Linux Foundation, among others, twenty-five companies in all, in publishing a letter titled "Open Weights and American AI Leadership," opposing restrictions Washington was reportedly considering on US companies using (especially Chinese) open-weight models, arguing the US keeps its AI lead by building an open model ecosystem, not by guarding a single best model. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang posted his first-ever post on X to promote the letter, racking up 11 million views within hours. The next day the signatory list doubled to 50, with new additions including OpenAI, Google, AMD, Cisco, Cloudflare, GitHub, and Ollama, and OpenAI and Google, both companies whose main business is closed models, chose to sign anyway. Never appearing on the list were Anthropic and Amazon (Amazon being Anthropic's largest investor), both companies that, like the signatories, depend on frontier model capability, and neither has publicly explained its absence.
items.why: 本期头条的直接背景：一版头条讲述 Anthropic 被指控欲禁止开源后亲自澄清，本条则介绍逼出其澄清的那封联署信——传播极快、声势浩大：一条推文 1100 万次浏览，一天内签署方翻倍，连主营闭源模型的 OpenAI 和谷歌都签了名，愈发凸显 Anthropic 和亚马逊沉默的分量。可迁移的判断：一份三页纸的联署信能在 24 小时内逼出整个行业的表态，说明当前科技政策战场很大程度上取决于谁先被看见、谁被迫跟进表态，而非缓慢协商的结果。
items.why_en: The direct backdrop to today's lead: the lead is about Anthropic stepping in to clarify itself after being accused of wanting to ban open weights, and this is about how fast and loud the letter that forced that clarification actually was, one tweet at 11 million views, signatories doubling in a day, even OpenAI and Google, both closed-model companies, signing on, which only makes Anthropic and Amazon's silence stand out more. The transferable judgment: a three-page letter forcing an entire industry to state a position within 24 hours shows today's tech policy battlefield is fought largely on who gets seen first and who's forced to react, not on slow negotiation.

items.title: 手机上把ChatGPT从Chat模式切到Work模式，代码解释器就能联网了
items.title_en: Flip ChatGPT mobile from Chat to Work mode and its Code Interpreter gets internet access
items.author: Simon Willison（点评 Ethan Mollick 的指南）
items.author_en: Simon Willison (commenting on Ethan Mollick's guide)
items.summary: Simon Willison 在博客上点评了 Ethan Mollick 那份“该用哪个 AI 做事”的指南一年来的变化。一年前，这份指南基本还在讲聊天模式：ChatGPT、Claude、Gemini，配上 o3、Claude 4 Opus、Gemini 2.5 Pro 这些模型，Deep Research 算是个有用的补充模式。今天的版本已经完全转向 agentic 系统。Mollick 的原话是，AI 能一口气干完相当于人类好几个小时的活。Gemini 这次直接从推荐名单里掉出去了，因为谷歌到现在都没有一个能跟 ChatGPT Work/Codex 或者 Claude Cowork/Code 对上号的成熟产品。Mollick 解释了怎么让 ChatGPT 或 Claude 用上你自己的电脑：用 AI 公司自己提供的云端电脑，模式叫 ChatGPT Work（在 ChatGPT 里）或者 Cowork（在 Claude 里）；真正给它接入你自己电脑权限的，是另外两个模式，ChatGPT 里叫 Work 和 Codex，Claude 里叫 Cowork 和 Code。这几个名字之间完全对不上，记不住很正常。Simon 自己补充了一个具体发现：手机上的 ChatGPT，如果把它从 Chat 模式切换到 Work 模式，它自带的代码解释器容器就不再被限制访问互联网了。跟桌面版比，这个反直觉的差异很少有人知道。
items.summary_en: Simon Willison used his blog to comment on how Ethan Mollick's guide to which AI to use has evolved over the past year. A year ago it was mostly about chat modes, ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, paired with o3, Claude 4 Opus, and Gemini 2.5 Pro, with Deep Research as a useful extra mode. Today's version has shifted fully to agentic systems, in Mollick's words, AI capable of doing the equivalent of many hours of human work in one go. Gemini dropped off the recommended list entirely this time because Google still doesn't have an established product matching ChatGPT Work/Codex or Claude Cowork/Code. Mollick explains how to give ChatGPT or Claude access to a computer: using the cloud computer the AI company itself provides, called ChatGPT Work (in ChatGPT) or Cowork (in Claude); the modes that give it access to your own computer are different ones, called Work and Codex in ChatGPT and Cowork and Code in Claude, names that don't map onto each other at all, so it's normal not to remember them. Simon added one concrete discovery of his own: on mobile ChatGPT, switching from Chat mode to Work mode removes the internet restriction on its built-in Code Interpreter container, a counterintuitive difference from the desktop app that few people know about.
items.why: 与前面几条关于“谁有权决定 AI 如何开放”的政策讨论完全不同，这是本期唯一一条纯工具/工作流条目。不管模型开源还是闭源，普通用户实际能不能用好它，取决于这些藏在命名里的细节。Simon 这条手机切 Work 模式解锁联网的发现就是个例子。可迁移的判断：与其等一个大而全的“哪个 AI 最好”的结论，不如像这样实测一下自己常用工具里那些同名不同义的模式，找出真正好用的那一个。今晚能做的事，见“今日上手”。
items.why_en: This sits on a completely different level from the earlier policy fight over who decides whether AI stays open, and it's the issue's one pure tool-and-workflow item: regardless of whether a model is open or closed, whether an ordinary user actually gets good use out of it depends on details hidden in mode names, and Simon's discovery about mobile Work mode unlocking internet access is exactly that. The transferable judgment: instead of waiting for one grand which-AI-is-best answer, test the same-named-but-different modes in the tools you already use, the way this does, and find the one that's actually good. Tonight's move: see hands_on.

items.title: Reid Hoffman和Mark Pincus新开的AI公司，卖的不是订阅，是省下来的钱
items.title_en: Reid Hoffman and Mark Pincus's new AI startup doesn't sell subscriptions, it sells savings
items.author: TechCrunch（经 TLDR AI 精选）
items.flag: ⚠️ 7500 万美元年化收入预测，以及 Hive-32B 模型跑赢 GPT-5.4 和 Claude Opus 4.6 的说法，来自媒体报道引用的投资材料，不是公开审计过的数字。融资本身也还在洽谈阶段，没有正式 close。
items.flag_en: ⚠️ The $75M ARR projection and the claim that Hive-32B beats GPT-5.4 and Claude Opus 4.6 come from investor materials cited by press reports, not audited public figures, and the funding round itself is still in talks, not closed.
items.summary: Prentis 是一家今年 4 月才成立的 AI 公司，创始人是连续创业者 Ritankar Das，联合创始人是 LinkedIn 联合创始人 Reid Hoffman 和把 Zynga 做大的 Mark Pincus。目前正在洽谈一轮 1 亿美元融资，估值 10 亿美元。公司做的是电脑操作模型：训练 AI 学会普通白领在处理保险理赔、清关关税异常这类跨文档、跨系统的日常流程时是怎么操作电脑的，目标是让 agent 能不靠人工介入，端到端接管这些工作。他们自己训练的 Hive-32B 模型，据称在电脑操作类基准上跑赢了 GPT-5.4 和 Claude Opus 4.6，每个任务的成本大约是这两家的十分之一。最值得留意的是它的收费方式：Prentis 不卖按坐席收费的订阅，而是抽成，从它的 agent 帮客户省下来的钱里抽 20%。据报道的投资材料显示，公司预计到今年三季度能做到 7500 万美元的年化收入。Hoffman 是 LinkedIn 联合创始人、Greylock 合伙人，也是 OpenAI 早期投资人，之前还跟 Mustafa Suleyman 一起创办过 Inflection AI（后来大部分团队被微软收编）。Pincus 则是把 Zynga 做成社交游戏巨头、后来卖掉的那个人，带来的是怎么把体验做得让人上瘾又好上手的经验。
items.summary_en: Prentis is an AI company founded just this April by serial entrepreneur Ritankar Das, co-founded with LinkedIn co-founder Reid Hoffman and Zynga builder Mark Pincus, currently in talks to raise $100M at a $1B valuation. It trains computer-use models: teaching AI how ordinary office workers operate their computers through cross-document, cross-system routine workflows like insurance claims and customs duty exceptions, aiming to let agents take those tasks over end to end without human intervention. Its own Hive-32B model reportedly beats GPT-5.4 and Claude Opus 4.6 on computer-use benchmarks at roughly a tenth of the per-task cost of either. The most notable detail is its pricing: Prentis doesn't sell per-seat subscriptions, it takes a 20% cut of whatever money its agents save the customer, and investor materials cited in reporting project a $75M annualized run rate by this year's third quarter. Hoffman, LinkedIn co-founder and Greylock partner, was an early OpenAI investor and previously co-founded Inflection AI with Mustafa Suleyman (later mostly absorbed by Microsoft); Pincus, who built Zynga into a social gaming giant before selling it, brings experience making experiences addictive and easy to pick up.
items.why: 本期唯一一条纯商业模式的条目，与头条那场“谁有资格开放模型”的争论完全岔开：不管上面吵成什么样，钱已经在往“按结果抽成”这种新定价模式流动，而不是按账号数订阅。可迁移的判断：如果你的产品里有一个功能是 AI 在真正干活、而不只是辅助人，订阅制未必是最好的收费方式，值得想一下有没有一个功能能改成按省下来的钱或者按完成的任务量抽成来试一次。今晚能做的事，见一版行动三。
items.why_en: The issue's one pure business-model item, entirely off to the side of the lead's fight over who gets to decide whether models stay open: whatever's happening up top, money is already flowing toward outcome-based pricing rather than per-seat subscriptions. The transferable judgment: if your product has a feature where AI is genuinely doing the work rather than just assisting, a subscription may not be the best way to charge for it, and it's worth considering whether one feature could be tested as a cut of savings or completed work instead. Tonight's move: see Action 3.
